candidate_relations.reason: Rheumatologic serologies were unremarkable and biopsy showed only nonspecific chronic synovitis rather than rheumatoid arthritis.
The sclerotic-rimmed cortical lesion in the femoral head is a bone tumor, but the label does not identify the osteoid osteoma subtype.
Normal inflammatory markers and negative cultures argue against osteomyelitis despite surrounding marrow edema.
A small well-defined cortical nidus with a thick sclerotic rim is not the destructive marrow pattern expected for bone lymphoma.
Only one femoral-head cortical lesion was found, with no recurrent multifocal osseous lesions supporting CRMO.
The repeat MRI localized a rimmed anterolateral cortical lesion rather than the geographic subchondral necrosis of avascular necrosis.
The lesion's sclerotic rim and cortical location are inconsistent with the typically expansile epiphyseal giant cell tumor.
No lytic skull or long-bone pattern or Langerhans-cell histology is present; biopsy instead sampled nonspecific synovium.
Six months of antitubercular therapy failed and all operative cultures were negative, while MRI later exposed a discrete cortical nidus.
Moderate effusion and synovitis were reactive, with no multiple intra-articular cartilaginous nodules to indicate synovial osteochondromatosis.
Normal ESR and CRP plus negative cultures do not support chronic osteomyelitis as the cause of the one-year pain.
Synovial histology lacked granulomas and empiric tuberculosis treatment produced no clinical benefit.
Imaging localized the abnormality to the femoral-head cortex, not a periarticular soft-tissue mass typical of synovial sarcoma.
Severe nocturnal hip pain and a well-defined cortical nidus surrounded by thick sclerosis identify osteoid osteoma.
The lymphoplasmacytic synovitis was nonspecific, with negative cultures and no response to prolonged antitubercular therapy.
Weight loss alone does not establish lymphoma when blood studies were normal and MRI demonstrated a classic focal cortical lesion.
The solitary anterolateral femoral-head lesion does not meet the multifocal distribution implied by chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis.
Neither synovial cultures nor histology demonstrated tuberculosis, and six months of therapy left the hip pain unchanged.
The MRI described a small rimmed cortical nidus without the expansile blood-filled architecture of an aneurysmal bone cyst.
Biopsy showed mild chronic synovitis without hemosiderin-laden proliferative tissue expected in pigmented villonodular synovitis.
